_comment: CENSYS PLATFORM (api.platform.censys.io / platform.censys.io) — the query language, the credit prices, and what each subscription tier is allowed to do. Censys retired the Legacy Search query language (`services.http.response.favicons.md5_hash`) in favour of CenQL, which namespaces every field under host. / web. / cert., so an old Censys query copied from a 2023 blog post will simply not run. Edit this file when Censys renames a field, changes a credit price, or when YOUR plan changes — the code holds only the matching logic, never the field names or the prices. Nothing here is case data: these are public product constants.

cenql_templates._comment: CenQL query templates, keyed by the ARTIFACT the query pivots on. `{value}` is substituted with the artifact value (already quoted where the template needs quotes). Several templates list more than one query because Censys splits the same fact across datasets: `web.` is the per-hostname:port web-property view, `host.` is the per-IP view, `cert.` is the certificate view. Run the `web.` form first for scam/phishing infrastructure (it is keyed on the hostname the victim sees); fall back to the `host.` form when you want every IP serving it. Verified against docs.censys.com (host / web-property / certificate datasets) 2026-08-04. OPERATOR CHOICE MATTERS: `=` is an exact, case-sensitive match (use it for hashes, fingerprints and whole hostnames) while `:` is a tokenised, case-insensitive match (use it for a bare subdomain LABEL or a body keyword, where an exact match on the whole field would find nothing). `=~` is regex and is Starter+ only, which is why no template here uses it.

pivot_kind_map._comment: WebPivot pivot `kind` -> the cenql_templates key that reverses it on Censys. A kind absent from this map simply gets no Censys query emitted — that is the correct outcome for artifacts Censys does not index (wallets, Telegram handles, phone numbers: use FOFA body= / PublicWWW / a search engine instead). Prefix keys ending in `:` match any kind starting with that prefix, so `tracker:` covers tracker:ga4, tracker:gtm and every future tracker subtype without editing this file.

credit_costs._comment: Censys Credits consumed per action on the Free and Starter tiers (docs.censys.com 'Credits for Free and Starter Users'). A Censys FREE account is granted `free_monthly_credits` per month and they DO NOT roll over. This is why WebPivot treats Censys as a metered API and skips it under --free-only: an entity lookup is cheap but a search is 5x the price, and 20 careless searches burn a whole month. `advanced_query` is any query using a regex (`=~`), which is Starter+ only anyway.

credit_budget._comment: THE SPEND GUARD. Censys is the tightest budget in the toolkit: 100 credits a MONTH on the free plan, no rollover, and a single careless sweep of 20 searches burns the entire month in one run — after which every Censys pivot in every other case is dead until the 1st. So `wp_censys` tracks what this month has already cost (summed from MEMORY/api_usage.jsonl, provider=censys) and refuses to spend past the budget instead of discovering the ceiling as an HTTP 402 mid-case. `monthly_credits` is the plan's grant — RAISE IT if you buy credits or upgrade (or set CENSYS_MONTHLY_CREDITS). `warn_at_remaining` is when the run starts printing the balance on every call, so the ceiling is visible before it is hit. `max_credits_per_run` is the per-process cap — a batch of 200 domains must not be able to spend a whole month on lookups nobody asked for; raise it deliberately for a run that genuinely needs it (CENSYS_MAX_CREDITS_PER_RUN), it is not a rate limit but a blast radius. `reserve_for_lookups` keeps a floor of credits that ONLY the 1-credit lookups may use, so an expensive search cannot consume the last of the month and leave the cheap cert-lookup — the highest-value free-plan call there is — unaffordable. Set `block_when_exhausted` false only if you would rather Censys answer 402 than skip.

plan_capabilities._comment: What each Censys subscription tier can actually do, so the tooling can degrade with an accurate message instead of an opaque 403. `api_search` is the one that matters most: on a FREE plan the Platform API exposes ONLY the lookup endpoints (host / web property / certificate, single + bulk) — POST /v3/global/search/query returns 403. A free analyst can still run any CenQL query by hand in the web UI (1 page of 100 results, 5 credits), which is why every Censys pivot also emits a platform.censys.io/search URL. Update these when Censys changes entitlements or when you upgrade.

free.note: API = lookup endpoints only (host / web property / certificate). Search via the web UI only.

starter.note: Reached by purchasing any amount of credits on a Free account. Unlocks the search API + regex.

core.note: Enterprise. JARM / JA4X / CensEye need the Adversary Investigation module on top.

adversary_investigation.note: Add-on module. The ONLY tier where JARM fingerprints and context hashes are searchable.

endpoints._comment: Censys Platform API v3 paths, relative to https://api.platform.censys.io. `lookup_*` are the FREE-tier endpoints (1 credit each; the bulk forms charge 1 credit per RESULT returned). `search_query` costs 5 credits and is Starter+. Authentication on all of them is `Authorization: Bearer <Personal Access Token>`, optionally scoped with the `X-Organization-ID` header. Verified live 2026-08-04.
